title: What sits between Revenue and Net Income?
introduction: Apple reported Revenue and Net Income for FY2025. Read the reported income-statement lines that connect the two figures.
boundary: This lesson follows Apple’s income statement. It does not show when cash moved, Apple’s cash balance, or the cash generated during the year.

total-cost-of-sales.helper: Cost recorded for the products and services Apple sold

gross-margin.helper: Apple’s label for this dollar subtotal; it is often called gross profit

total-operating-expenses.helper: Research and development plus selling, general and administrative expenses

operating-income.helper: After cost of sales and operating expenses

other-income-expense-net.helper: A signed line; it was negative in FY2025

income-before-income-taxes.reportedLabel: Income before provision for income taxes
income-before-income-taxes.helper: The subtotal before Apple’s income tax provision

income-tax-provision.helper: Accounting tax expense, not necessarily cash tax paid during the year

net-income.helper: The final Profit line used in this lesson

stages.traceBody: Apple’s filing labels Revenue as Total net sales. The reported costs and expenses below it determine the later Profit lines.
stages.traceBoundary: Revenue alone cannot tell you Net Income.

stages.traceBody: Apple labels this dollar subtotal Gross margin. The same amount is often called gross profit.
stages.traceBoundary: This is an amount, not the Gross Margin percentage.

stages.continueLabel: Continue to the final reported lines
stages.traceHeading: Operating income is not the final line.
stages.traceBody: Apple reported Operating income after cost of sales and operating expenses.
stages.traceBoundary: Other income or expense and income tax still sit between this subtotal and Net income.

stages.navigationLabel: Other item, tax and final line
stages.traceHeading: Net income is the final Profit line used here.
stages.traceBody: Other income/(expense), net reduced Apple’s FY2025 income before tax. After its income tax provision, Apple reported Net income.
stages.traceBoundary: Net income is an accounting result. It is not cash held or cash generated.

question.prompt: Revenue rises next year, but costs and expenses rise even faster. What could happen to Net Income?
question.hint: Choose one. This is practice, not a score.
question.supportedFeedback: Yes. Revenue is the starting line. If costs and expenses grow faster, Net Income may be lower.
question.unsupportedFeedback: Revenue alone does not decide Net Income. Costs, expenses, other income or expense, and tax can change too.

verification.unitNote: Apple reports USD millions. FinPath displays the same values in USD billions.
verification.displayNote: Minus and plus signs organize the learning calculation. The exact record preserves Apple’s reported line names and signed other-income/expense amount.

nextPreview: Next: Profit Margin — compare Net Income with Revenue to ask how much Net Income Apple reported for every $100 of Revenue.
